definition_zh: 齿槽的；肺泡的；（语音）齿龈音的；齿龈音
definition_en: relating to the tooth sockets, the air sacs of the lungs, or a sound made with the tongue near the ridge behind the upper teeth
core_image: 身体里一排排盛着牙、盛着气的小凹槽
scene: 牙科诊室里医生指着片子向病人讲解。The dentist said the tooth was firmly set in its alveolar socket.
sceneCN: 这里的 alveolar 是「齿槽的」（第 1 个义项：与牙槽相关的）；句意是牙医说这颗牙牢牢长在牙槽窝里。

pos.zh: 齿槽的；肺泡的；齿龈音的

derivatives.zh: 由同一名词单数而来，义为「小凹槽；牙槽；肺泡」
alveolus 的复数形式，常指肺泡
由 alveolus 加形容词后缀构成，义为「蜂窝状的」

senses.title: Relating to the sockets of the teeth
senses.titleCN: 齿槽的：与牙槽相关
senses.definition: of or connected with the bony socket in the jaw that holds a tooth
senses.definitionCN: 与下颌中容纳牙齿的骨质牙槽相关的
senses.example: Gum disease can damage the alveolar bone that supports the teeth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙龈疾病会破坏支撑牙齿的牙槽骨。
senses.why: The word names the little hollow in the jaw where each tooth sits, so dentistry uses it for everything around that socket.
senses.whyCN: 这个词本义指颌骨上容纳牙齿的小凹窝，牙科因此用它指代牙槽周围的一切结构。

senses.title: Relating to the air sacs of the lungs
senses.titleCN: 肺泡的：与肺部气囊相关
senses.definition: of or connected with the tiny air sacs in the lungs where gas exchange happens
senses.definitionCN: 与肺中进行气体交换的微小气囊相关的
senses.example: Oxygen passes from the alveolar sacs into the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 氧气从肺泡囊进入血液。
senses.why: The lungs are full of little hollows, and the same word for a small cavity was applied to them.
senses.whyCN: 肺里布满小空腔，表示「小凹窝」的同一个词便被借用来称呼它们。

senses.title: Made with the tongue at the ridge behind the upper teeth
senses.titleCN: 齿龈音的：舌抵上齿龈发出的
senses.definition: in phonetics, describing a sound produced with the tongue touching or near the ridge behind the upper front teeth
senses.definitionCN: 语音学中指舌尖抵住或接近上齿龈嵴发出的音
senses.example: The English t and d are alveolar stops.
senses.exampleCN: 英语的 t 和 d 是齿龈塞音。
senses.why: The ridge behind the teeth is the bony alveolar ridge, so sounds made there took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 牙齿后方的骨嵴就叫牙槽嵴，在该处发出的音便沿用了同一个名称。

senses.title: An alveolar speech sound as a noun
senses.titleCN: 齿龈音（名词）
senses.definition: a speech sound, such as t, d, n, or s, produced at the alveolar ridge
senses.definitionCN: 在齿龈嵴处发出的语音，如 t、d、n、s
senses.example: This dialect drops the final alveolar in many words.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方言在许多词里丢掉末尾的齿龈音。
senses.why: Once the adjective named the place of articulation, it was turned into a noun for any sound made there.
senses.whyCN: 形容词命名了发音部位之后，它又转为名词，指在该部位发出的任何音。

senses.title: Relating to the alveolar bone tissue
senses.titleCN: 牙槽骨组织的
senses.definition: of the specialized bone of the jaws that anchors the teeth
senses.definitionCN: 指颌骨中锚定牙齿的特殊骨质
senses.example: Implants fuse with the alveolar tissue over several months.
senses.exampleCN: 种植体在几个月内与牙槽组织融合。
senses.why: Because the socket is bone, the adjective extends to the bone substance itself.
senses.whyCN: 牙槽本身就是骨质，形容词因此扩展到骨质本身。

senses.title: Shaped like or relating to small glandular pockets
senses.titleCN: 腺泡状的：指小囊状腺体
senses.definition: in anatomy, describing glands composed of small sac-like cavities
senses.definitionCN: 解剖学中形容由小囊状空腔构成的腺体
senses.example: The salivary gland contains alveolar structures that store secretion.
senses.exampleCN: 唾液腺中含有储存分泌物的腺泡状结构。
senses.why: Any cluster of tiny cavities in the body recalls the original hollow, so the word spreads to gland anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 体内任何小腔室簇都让人想起最初的「小凹窝」，这个词便扩展到腺体解剖。

senses.title: Relating to gas pressure inside the lungs
senses.titleCN: 肺泡气压的
senses.definition: of the pressure or gas measured within the pulmonary air sacs
senses.definitionCN: 指在肺部气囊内测得的气压或气体
senses.example: Alveolar pressure falls as the chest expands during inhalation.
senses.exampleCN: 吸气时胸廓扩张，肺泡内压下降。
senses.why: Physiology measures what happens inside the air sacs, and the adjective follows the location.
senses.whyCN: 生理学要测量气囊内部发生的变化，形容词便随部位一起被使用。

senses.title: Relating to small hollows in general
senses.titleCN: 泛指小凹窝的
senses.definition: describing any small cavity or pitted structure, especially in scientific description
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何小空腔或蜂窝状结构，尤用于科学描述
senses.example: The fossil bone shows an alveolar surface under the microscope.
senses.exampleCN: 显微镜下，这块化石骨呈现蜂窝状的表面。
senses.why: Back to the root meaning, anything pitted with little hollows can be called by this word.
senses.whyCN: 回到词根本义，凡是布满小凹窝的结构都可以用这个词形容。

intro.en: Alveolar comes from Latin alveolus, a diminutive of alveus meaning hollow or small cavity, later specialized in anatomy and phonetics.
intro.cn: alveolar 源自拉丁语 alveolus，它是 alveus（凹陷、腹腔）的指小形式，后专门用于解剖学和语音学。

items.en: A root meaning hollow or container, generally reconstructed for alveus.
items.cn: 一般认为 alveus 来自表示「凹陷、容器」的重构词根。

items.en: alveus, "hollow, belly, bed of a river".
items.cn: 拉丁语 alveus「凹陷；腹腔；河床」。

items.en: alveolus, "a little hollow", used for small pits and cavities.
items.cn: 拉丁语指小形式 alveolus「小凹窝」，用于指小坑与空腔。

items.en: alveolaris, formed in anatomical writing for the tooth sockets.
items.cn: 新拉丁语 alveolaris，在解剖学文献中用于指牙槽。

items.en: English alveolar appears in anatomy for tooth sockets and lung sacs.
items.cn: 十八世纪英语 alveolar 进入解剖学，指牙槽和肺泡。

items.en: Phonetics later borrowed it for sounds made at the alveolar ridge.
items.cn: 语音学随后借它指在齿龈嵴处发出的音。

note.en: Distinguish alveolar from its parent word alveolus and from look-alike words that share only the al- spelling.
note.cn: 要把 alveolar 与母词 alveolus 区分开，也要与只是拼写相近的 al- 开头词区分。

entries.definition: the parent noun: a small cavity, especially a tooth socket or lung air sac.
entries.definitionCN: 母词：小凹窝，尤指牙槽或肺泡。

entries.definition: an entirely different Arabic-derived word that merely begins with al-.
entries.definitionCN: 词源完全不同的阿拉伯语借词，只是同样以 al- 开头，形近而已。

entries.definition: the plural of alveolus, the standard term for the lung air sacs.
entries.definitionCN: alveolus 的复数，是「肺泡」的标准说法。

entries.definition: relating to the teeth themselves rather than their sockets.
entries.definitionCN: 指牙齿本身，而非容纳牙齿的牙槽。

entries.definition: a phonetic term for sounds made at the hard palate, near but behind the alveolar ridge.
entries.definitionCN: 语音学术语，指在上腭发出的音，位置在齿龈嵴之后。

entries.definition: relating to the lungs as a whole, of which the alveoli are part.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个肺，肺泡只是肺的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Remember alveolar through its root idea of a little hollow.
normalIntro.cn: 通过「小凹窝」这个词根意象记住 alveolar。

normal.en: alveus (hollow) + -olus (little) + -ar (of): of the little hollows.
normal.cn: alveus（凹陷）+ -olus（小）+ -ar（……的）：属于小凹窝的。

normal.en: Each tooth sits in its own little hollow: the alveolar socket.
normal.cn: 每颗牙都坐在自己的小凹窝里：牙槽窝。

normal.en: The lungs look like bunches of tiny hollow grapes: alveoli.
normal.cn: 肺像一串串小空心葡萄：肺泡。

normal.en: Say t or d: your tongue touches the bony ridge, the alveolar ridge.
normal.cn: 发 t 或 d 时，舌尖正抵着那道骨嵴——齿龈嵴。

normal.en: Family chain: alveus → alveolus → alveolar, from hollow to little hollow to adjective.
normal.cn: 词族链：alveus → alveolus → alveolar，从凹窝到小凹窝再到形容词。

abstract.en: Picture an egg carton: every tooth rests in one dimple.
abstract.cn: 想象一个蛋托：每颗牙都安放在一个小凹槽里。

abstract.en: Imagine thousands of tiny bubbles inside the lungs filling with air.
abstract.cn: 想象肺里成千上万个微小的气泡正被空气充满。

abstract.en: Feel your tongue tap the ridge just behind your top teeth.
abstract.cn: 感觉舌尖轻叩上门牙后方的骨嵴。

examples.en: Smoking destroys the delicate alveolar walls of the lungs.
examples.cn: 吸烟会破坏肺部脆弱的肺泡壁。

examples.en: The s sound is a voiceless alveolar fricative.
examples.cn: 音 s 是清齿龈擦音。

examples.en: Bone loss in the alveolar ridge loosened the tooth.
examples.cn: 牙槽嵴骨质流失使牙齿松动。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艾尔维尔」——艾尔维尔满口凹槽牙，一笑就露出两排小窝窝。

root: 拉丁语 alveus（凹陷、腹腔）加指小后缀 -olus 构成 alveolus（小凹窝），再接形容词后缀 -ar 得 alveolar，字面义为「属于小凹窝的」。牙槽、肺泡、齿龈嵴都因形似小凹窝而得名。

sensesIntro.en: From the basic idea of a little hollow, the senses spread to tooth sockets, lung sacs, the speech ridge, and the sounds made there.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「小凹窝」这一基本意象出发，义项扩展到牙槽、肺泡、齿龈嵴以及在该处发出的语音。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of little hollows holding teeth or air
core.cn: 核心意象：一排排盛着牙或盛着气的小凹窝

branches.en: The socket of a tooth in the jaw.
branches.cn: 颌骨中容纳牙齿的牙槽。

branches.en: The air sacs of the lungs and what is measured inside them.
branches.cn: 肺部气囊及其内部测得的气压。

branches.en: The ridge behind the teeth as a place of articulation.
branches.cn: 作为发音部位的齿龈嵴。

branches.en: Any consonant produced at that ridge.
branches.cn: 在该嵴处发出的任何辅音。

branches.en: Bone tissue, glandular pockets, and small hollows in general.
branches.cn: 骨组织、腺泡状结构与泛指的小凹窝。

intro.en: Alveolar is a transparent Latin diminutive plus an adjective suffix.
intro.cn: alveolar 由拉丁语指小形式加形容词后缀清晰构成。

latinIntro.en: The base alveus traveled intact from Latin into modern anatomical Latin.
latinIntro.cn: 词基 alveus 从拉丁语完整进入现代解剖学拉丁语。

latinEntries.example: alveoli pulmonum in Latin anatomical texts
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁解剖学文献中的 alveoli pulmonum（肺泡）

definition_zh: 积聚；积累；聚集；堆积
definition_en: to gather together or collect a large amount of something over time
core_image: 雪球越滚越大：一点一点把东西拢成一大堆
scene: 老人坐在账本前清点一生攒下的家产。Over decades he managed to amass a huge fortune.
sceneCN: 这里的 amass 是「积聚」（第 1 个义项：逐渐积累大量财富）；句意是他几十年间攒下了一大笔财富。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「积聚；聚积之物」，较少用
词根词，义为「团；块；大量」
由 mass 加形容词后缀构成，义为「巨大的」

senses.title: To accumulate wealth over time
senses.titleCN: 积聚财富
senses.definition: to gradually gather a large amount of money or property
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐聚集大量钱财或资产
senses.example: She amassed a fortune in the shipping trade.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠航运业积攒了一笔巨款。
senses.why: Wealth is pictured as loose coins being gathered into one great mass.
senses.whyCN: 财富被想象成散落的钱币被拢成一大堆。

senses.title: To collect a large quantity of things
senses.titleCN: 大量收集物品
senses.definition: to bring together a large number of objects or items
senses.definitionCN: 把大量物件汇集到一起
senses.example: The museum has amassed a remarkable collection of old maps.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆汇集了一大批珍贵的老地图收藏。
senses.why: The same gathering image applies to any objects piled into one place.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「聚拢」意象适用于堆在一处的任何物品。

senses.title: To gather information or evidence
senses.titleCN: 汇集信息或证据
senses.definition: to accumulate facts, data, or proof in quantity
senses.definitionCN: 大量积累事实、数据或证据
senses.example: Lawyers amassed enough evidence to reopen the case.
senses.exampleCN: 律师们收集到足够的证据使案件重审。
senses.why: Abstract items are treated like a pile that grows heavier piece by piece.
senses.whyCN: 抽象事物被当作一堆逐件增重的物质来对待。

senses.title: To assemble people or troops
senses.titleCN: 集结人员或军队
senses.definition: to bring soldiers or crowds together in one place
senses.definitionCN: 把士兵或人群召集到一处
senses.example: The general amassed his troops on the northern border.
senses.exampleCN: 将军在北部边境集结了军队。
senses.why: A crowd, like matter, forms one dense mass when gathered.
senses.whyCN: 人群和物质一样，聚集起来便形成一个密集的群体。

senses.title: To pile up as debts or problems
senses.titleCN: 堆积（债务、问题等负面事物）
senses.definition: to accumulate something undesirable, such as debt or trouble
senses.definitionCN: 积累债务、麻烦等不良事物
senses.example: The company amassed huge debts before collapsing.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司在倒闭前积欠了巨额债务。
senses.why: The mass can be heavy in a bad way; the verb stays neutral and the context turns negative.
senses.whyCN: 「一大堆」也可以是坏的重负，动词本身中性，由语境转贬。

senses.title: To accumulate naturally or by deposit
senses.titleCN: 自然堆积
senses.definition: to build up gradually as matter settles or collects, as with snow or dust
senses.definitionCN: 如雪、尘等物质沉降聚集而逐渐增厚
senses.example: Grey dust had amassed on the abandoned shelves.
senses.exampleCN: 废弃的书架上积了厚厚的灰尘。
senses.why: Without human agency, small particles still merge into a mass.
senses.whyCN: 无需人力，细小颗粒也会聚成一体。

senses.title: To gather knowledge or experience
senses.titleCN: 积累知识或经验
senses.definition: to acquire a large store of learning or practical skill over the years
senses.definitionCN: 多年间积累大量学识或经验
senses.example: He amassed a lifetime of wisdom working in the village clinic.
senses.exampleCN: 他在乡村诊所工作中积累了一生的智慧。
senses.why: Knowledge is stored like grain in a barn, a heap added to year after year.
senses.whyCN: 知识像谷仓里的粮堆，年复一年地添高。

senses.title: To crowd together physically
senses.titleCN: （人、物）密集聚集
senses.definition: to form a dense crowd or heap in one place
senses.definitionCN: 在一处形成密集的人群或堆
senses.example: Protesters amassed outside the city hall all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 抗议者整个上午都在市政厅外聚集。
senses.why: The intransitive use shows the mass forming by itself.
senses.whyCN: 不及物用法显示这个「团块」自行形成。

intro.en: Amass joins the Latin prefix ad- (to) with massa (lump, mass), passing through Old French into English.
intro.cn: amass 由拉丁语前缀 ad-（朝向）加 massa（团、块）构成，经古法语进入英语。

items.en: maza, "barley cake, lump", a likely relative of mass.
items.cn: 希腊语 maza「大麦饼、团块」，一般认为是 mass 的亲戚（重构形式）。

items.en: massa, "lump of dough, mass".
items.cn: 拉丁语 massa「面团；团块」。

items.en: amasser, "to gather into a mass", from a- (from ad-) plus masser.
items.cn: 古法语 amasser「聚成一团」，由 a-（来自 ad-）加 masser 构成。

items.en: English amass appears in the fifteenth century with the sense of gathering into a heap.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语 amass 出现，义为聚集成堆。

items.en: Now the standard verb for accumulating wealth, data, or forces in quantity.
items.cn: 如今是表示大量积累财富、数据或力量的标准动词。

note.en: Distinguish amass from its root mass and from near synonyms of accumulating.
note.cn: 要把 amass 与词根词 mass 以及表示积累的近义词区分开。

entries.definition: the root noun: a large body of matter or quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 词根名词：团、块、大量。

entries.definition: a Greek-derived medical word sharing only the a-m spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊语来源的医学词，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: adjective from mass, meaning very large and heavy.
entries.definitionCN: 由 mass 派生的形容词，义为巨大的。

entries.definition: to pile up gradually, stressing slow increase.
entries.definitionCN: 逐渐累积，强调缓慢增加。

entries.definition: to amass and secretly store away, often selfishly.
entries.definitionCN: 积藏并私自储存，常含吝啬意味。

entries.definition: to accumulate a reserve supply for future use.
entries.definitionCN: 囤积备用物资。

normalIntro.en: Remember amass through its two building blocks.
normalIntro.cn: 通过两个构件记住 amass。

normal.en: a- (to) + mass: to gather into one mass.
normal.cn: a-（朝向）+ mass（团块）：聚成一大团。

normal.en: Think of a snowball rolling downhill, adding mass as it goes.
normal.cn: 想想滚下山的雪球，一路越滚越大。

normal.en: Family chain: mass → massive → amass, from lump to huge to gathered-up.
normal.cn: 词族链：mass → massive → amass，从团块到巨大到聚集成堆。

normal.en: Amass usually implies quantity built over time, not a single act.
normal.cn: amass 通常指长期积累的量，而非一次动作。

normal.en: Common partners: fortune, wealth, data, troops, debts.
normal.cn: 常见搭配对象：财富、钱财、数据、军队、债务。

abstract.en: Picture coins sliding off a table into one heavy pile.
abstract.cn: 想象硬币从桌上滑落，堆成沉甸甸的一堆。

abstract.en: See dust settling layer upon layer on a quiet shelf.
abstract.cn: 看灰尘一层层落在安静的书架上。

abstract.en: Watch soldiers streaming in from all roads to one field.
abstract.cn: 看士兵从各条道路汇聚到同一片旷野。

examples.en: He amassed millions of followers within two years.
examples.cn: 他在两年内积累了数百万粉丝。

examples.en: The team amassed a huge body of research data.
examples.cn: 团队积累了庞大的研究数据。

examples.en: Clouds amassed on the horizon before the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴前，云在地平线上聚拢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿马斯」——阿马斯一口气把满屋金币扫成一大堆，越堆越高。

root: 拉丁语前缀 ad-（朝向）在 m 前变为 a-，加 massa（团块，一般源自希腊语 maza「大麦饼」）构成古法语 amasser「聚成一团」，进入英语后为 amass，字面义为「使成一大团」。一般认为希腊词源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: From gathering things into one heap, the senses spread to wealth, data, troops, debts, and natural deposits.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把东西聚成一堆出发，义项扩展到财富、数据、军队、债务与自然沉积。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: loose things gathered into one heavy heap
core.cn: 核心意象：散落之物聚成沉重的一堆

branches.en: Money and property piling up over time.
branches.cn: 钱财资产随时间不断堆积。

branches.en: Objects, data, and evidence gathered in bulk.
branches.cn: 物品、数据与证据的大量汇集。

branches.en: People or troops forming one dense mass.
branches.cn: 人群或军队聚成密集的群体。

branches.en: The heap as a burden of debt or trouble.
branches.cn: 堆成的债务或麻烦等重负。

branches.en: Natural deposits and slowly stored knowledge.
branches.cn: 自然沉积与慢慢储存的知识。

intro.en: Amass is a Latin prefix fused to a mass root.
intro.cn: amass 由拉丁语前缀与词根 mass 融合而成。

latinIntro.en: The root massa passed from Greek through Latin and French into English.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 massa 经希腊语、拉丁语和法语进入英语。

definition_zh: 爱情的；恋爱的；与性爱有关的
definition_en: relating to love, especially sexual love
core_image: 写着情诗的鹅毛笔：专为爱情而生的词
scene: 书房里诗人正在为心上人写下情诗。He kept his amatory verses hidden in a locked drawer.
sceneCN: 这里的 amatory 是「爱情的」（第 1 个义项：与恋爱有关的）；句意是他把情诗藏在锁着的抽屉里。

derivatives.zh: 同族名词，义为「爱好者；业余爱好者」，源自同一拉丁词根
同族形容词，义为「多情的；含情脉脉的」
由 amor 加名词后缀构成，义为「写情爱题材的作家；多情的人」

senses.title: Relating to love or courtship
senses.titleCN: 爱情的：与恋爱求爱相关
senses.definition: connected with romantic love or the act of courtship
senses.definitionCN: 与浪漫爱情或求爱行为相关的
senses.example: The poet is famous for his amatory sonnets.
senses.exampleCN: 这位诗人以爱情十四行诗闻名。
senses.why: The Latin root amor means love, and the adjective simply marks anything devoted to it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语词根 amor 意为爱，形容词只是标记一切与爱情有关的事物。

senses.title: Expressing sexual desire
senses.titleCN: 性爱的：表达情欲
senses.definition: expressing or suggesting physical passion between lovers
senses.definitionCN: 表达或暗示恋人间的肉体情欲
senses.example: The novel contains several amatory scenes.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说里有几段情爱描写。
senses.why: Latin amor covered desire as well as affection, so the adjective keeps both colors.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 amor 兼指欲望与爱慕，这个形容词因此保留两层色彩。

senses.title: Characteristic of a lover
senses.titleCN: 恋人般的：具有恋人姿态的
senses.definition: having the manner or style typical of a lover courting someone
senses.definitionCN: 具有求爱者典型举止或风格的
senses.example: He gave her an amatory glance across the table.
senses.exampleCN: 他隔着桌子向她投去含情的一瞥。
senses.why: From describing love poetry, the word widened to describing loving behavior.
senses.whyCN: 从描述爱情诗扩展到描述示爱的行为举止。

senses.title: Relating to love affairs in literature
senses.titleCN: 言情题材的（文学）
senses.definition: in literary criticism, describing works built on romantic plots
senses.definitionCN: 文学批评中形容以恋爱情节为主线的作品
senses.example: Amatory fiction flourished in eighteenth-century England.
senses.exampleCN: 言情小说在十八世纪的英国盛极一时。
senses.why: Critics needed a compact label for the love-plot genre, and the Latin adjective served.
senses.whyCN: 批评家需要一个简洁标签指称言情体裁，拉丁语形容词便派上用场。

senses.title: Devoted to the pursuit of love
senses.titleCN: 沉溺恋爱的：热衷求爱的
senses.definition: given to or occupied with romantic adventures
senses.definitionCN: 醉心于恋爱韵事或情感冒险的
senses.example: The hero leads an amatory life through half of Europe.
senses.exampleCN: 主人公在半个欧洲过着猎艳般的风流生活。
senses.why: When a person rather than a text is described, the sense becomes a habitual pursuit.
senses.whyCN: 当描述对象从文本换成人物时，词义变成一种惯常的追逐。

senses.title: Relating to the emotion of love in general
senses.titleCN: 泛指爱恋情感的
senses.definition: of the feelings of attachment and affection between people
senses.definitionCN: 泛指人与人之间的依恋与爱慕之情
senses.example: Her letters reveal an amatory turmoil of youth.
senses.exampleCN: 她的信件透露出年轻时情感上的纷乱。
senses.why: Beyond physical desire, the word can name the whole emotional state of loving.
senses.whyCN: 超出肉体欲望之外，这个词也能指称恋爱情感的整个状态。

intro.en: Amatory comes from Latin amor (love), the root that also gives amateur and amorous.
intro.cn: amatory 源自拉丁语 amor（爱），与 amateur、amorous 同根。

items.en: A root meaning to love or desire, generally reconstructed as *am-.
items.cn: 一般认为源自表示「爱、欲」的重构词根 *am-。

items.en: amor, "love", and amatorius, "of a lover, loving".
items.cn: 拉丁语 amor「爱」；amatorius「恋人的；钟情的」。

items.en: amatorius used by classical authors for love poetry and lovers.
items.cn: 古典作家用 amatorius 形容情诗与恋人。

items.en: English amatory appears in the sixteenth century in learned writing.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 amatory 出现于学术性书面语。

items.en: Now a literary word for anything concerning love, especially in formal description.
items.cn: 如今是书面语词，指一切与爱情有关的事物，尤用于正式描述。

note.en: Distinguish amatory from its root family amor/amateur/amorous and from look-alike am- words.
note.cn: 要把 amatory 与词族 amor/amateur/amorous 区分开，也要与形近的 am- 开头词区分。

entries.definition: same Latin root, but stressing being in love or showing desire.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词，更强调「坠入爱河、流露情欲」的状态。

entries.definition: same root: one who does something for the love of it, a non-professional.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词：因喜爱而做某事的人，即非职业爱好者。

entries.definition: a different Latin word sharing only the am- spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 另一个拉丁语词，只是拼写开头相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: relating to love with an idealized, imaginative coloring.
entries.definitionCN: 指带有理想化、浪漫想象色彩的爱情。

entries.definition: more explicit term for sexual desire or arousal.
entries.definitionCN: 更直接指性欲与情欲的词。

entries.definition: full of strong feeling, not only of the romantic kind.
entries.definitionCN: 充满强烈情感的，不限于爱情。

normalIntro.en: Remember amatory through its Latin root of love.
normalIntro.cn: 通过拉丁语词根「爱」记住 amatory。

normal.en: amor (love) + -atory (of): of love.
normal.cn: amor（爱）+ -atory（与……有关）：爱情的。

normal.en: Same root as amorous and amateur: all grew from love.
normal.cn: 与 amorous、amateur 同根：都源自「爱」。

normal.en: An amateur works for love of it; amatory works are about love.
normal.cn: amateur 为爱而做；amatory 写的正是爱。

normal.en: Think of Cupid, the little god of amor.
normal.cn: 想想丘比特——掌管 amor 的小爱神。

normal.en: It is a bookish word: amatory verse, amatory fiction, amatory adventures.
normal.cn: 它是书面语词：常见于 amatory verse、amatory fiction、amatory adventures。

abstract.en: Picture a quill pen dipping into red ink to write a love poem.
abstract.cn: 想象一支鹅毛笔蘸着红墨水写情诗。

abstract.en: See Cupid drawing his bow over a stack of love letters.
abstract.cn: 看丘比特在一摞情书上方张弓搭箭。

abstract.en: Feel the hush of a candlelit room where a sonnet is read aloud.
abstract.cn: 感受烛光房间里有人轻声朗读情诗的静谧。

examples.en: The anthology collects amatory poetry from six centuries.
examples.cn: 这部选集收录了六个世纪的爱情诗。

examples.en: Their amatory correspondence was discovered years later.
examples.cn: 多年后他们的情书往来被发现。

examples.en: Critics regard it as a landmark of amatory fiction.
examples.cn: 评论界视其为言情小说的里程碑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿玛托丽」——阿玛托丽姑娘人人爱，她的名字写满了情书。

root: 拉丁语 amor（爱，一般认为源自重构词根 *am-「爱、欲」）派生形容词 amatorius（恋爱的），进入英语后为 amatory，字面义为「属于爱的」。同族词有 amorous（多情的）、amateur（爱好者）。

sensesIntro.en: From love poetry, the senses extend to desire, loving behavior, the romance genre, and a life of courtship.
sensesIntro.cn: 从爱情诗出发，义项扩展到情欲、示爱行为、言情体裁与风流生涯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pen devoted only to writing about love
core.cn: 核心意象：一支专为爱情而动的笔

branches.en: Love and courtship in general, as in love poetry.
branches.cn: 泛指爱情与求爱，如情诗。

branches.en: Physical desire and the whole emotional state of loving.
branches.cn: 肉体情欲与恋爱情感的整体状态。

branches.en: The manner typical of a lover.
branches.cn: 恋人特有的举止神态。

branches.en: The literary genre built on romantic plots.
branches.cn: 以恋爱情节为主线的文学体裁。

branches.en: A life given to romantic adventures.
branches.cn: 醉心恋爱韵事的生涯。

intro.en: Amatory is a Latin love root with a learned adjective suffix.
intro.cn: amatory 由拉丁语「爱」词根加学术性形容词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root amor passed directly from Latin into learned English vocabulary.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 amor 直接从拉丁语进入英语学术词汇。

items.meaning: one who, of the nature of
items.exampleCN: 见拉丁语 amatorius、英语 amatory

latinEntries.example: amor vincit omnia in Latin verse
latinEntries.exampleCN: 拉丁诗句 amor vincit omnia（爱征服一切）
古典拉丁语中的 carmina amatoria（情诗）

definition_zh: 矛盾的；态度摇摆的；有好几种对立感情的
definition_en: having mixed or contradictory feelings about someone or something at the same time
core_image: 心里两个小人打架：既想靠近又想躲开
scene: 她在旧居门前徘徊，手放在门把上又缩回来。She felt ambivalent about selling the family house.
sceneCN: 这里的 ambivalent 是「矛盾的」（第 1 个义项：同时怀有两种对立情感）；句意是她对卖掉祖屋心情矛盾。

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「矛盾心理；摇摆态度」
由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「矛盾地；摇摆地」
同缀词，由 equi- 加 -valent 构成，义为「等价的」，可对照记忆

senses.title: Having mixed feelings toward a person or thing
senses.titleCN: 对人对事怀有矛盾情感
senses.definition: experiencing two opposed emotions, such as love and dislike, toward the same object at the same time
senses.definitionCN: 对同一对象同时怀有两种对立情绪，如又爱又厌
senses.example: He was ambivalent about his promotion: proud, yet uneasy.
senses.exampleCN: 他对升职心情矛盾：既自豪又不安。
senses.why: Two valences pull on the same person, and both are held at once.
senses.whyCN: 两种「价」同时拉扯同一个人，且被同时握有。

senses.title: Undecided between two courses of action
senses.titleCN: 在两种选择间摇摆不定
senses.definition: unable to settle on one of two alternatives because both attract and repel
senses.definitionCN: 因两案各有吸引力又各有排斥而难以抉择
senses.example: Voters remain ambivalent between the two candidates.
senses.exampleCN: 选民在两位候选人之间犹豫不决。
senses.why: The internal tug-of-war shows outward as hesitation between options.
senses.whyCN: 内心的拉锯外化为在选项之间的犹豫。

senses.title: Sending out contradictory signals
senses.titleCN: 释放矛盾信号的
senses.definition: appearing to approve and disapprove at the same time in words or behavior
senses.definitionCN: 言行上似乎同时表示赞同与反对
senses.example: The ministry gave an ambivalent response to the proposal.
senses.exampleCN: 部委对该提案给出了含混矛盾的回应。
senses.why: When applied to institutions, the inner conflict becomes visible contradiction.
senses.whyCN: 用于机构时，内在冲突表现为可见的自相矛盾。

senses.title: Valued in two different ways
senses.titleCN: 兼具两种价值的
senses.definition: in psychology, describing an object or bond that carries both attraction and aversion
senses.definitionCN: 心理学中形容同时带有吸引与排斥的对象或关系
senses.example: The child showed an ambivalent attachment to her caregiver.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子对照顾者表现出矛盾的依恋。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the two-valence image in a measurable form.
senses.whyCN: 术语义把「两种价」的意象保留为可测量的形式。

senses.title: Interpretable in two opposite readings
senses.titleCN: 可作两种对立解读的
senses.definition: of a text or symbol open to two conflicting interpretations
senses.definitionCN: 指文本或符号可作两种相互冲突的解读
senses.example: The ending is ambivalent: triumph or surrender?
senses.exampleCN: 结尾是两可的：是胜利还是屈服？
senses.why: Meaning, too, can carry two valences, and readers must weigh both.
senses.whyCN: 意义同样可以带两种「价」，读者必须两者权衡。

senses.title: Simultaneously drawn to and wary of a culture or idea
senses.titleCN: 对文化、观念既向往又警惕的
senses.definition: describing a group's or person's attraction and distrust toward an idea or culture
senses.definitionCN: 形容群体或个人对某一观念、文化既向往又戒备
senses.example: The novel captures a generation ambivalent about modernity.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说捕捉到一代人对现代性的矛盾心态。
senses.why: Whole societies, like individuals, can hold two valences about big ideas.
senses.whyCN: 整个社会如同个人，也会对宏大观念同时持有两种态度。

intro.en: Ambivalent joins Latin ambi- (both ways) with valentia (power, capacity), coined in early twentieth-century psychology.
intro.cn: ambivalent 由拉丁语 ambi-（两方）加 valentia（力量、能力）构成，是二十世纪初心理学的造词。

items.en: ambi-, "both, on both sides", and valere, "to be strong".
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambi-「两边的」；valere「强壮、有力」。

items.en: valentia, "power, capacity", later a term in chemistry and physics.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 valentia「力量、能力」，后成为化学、物理术语。

items.en: Psychologist Eugen Bleuler formed Ambivalenz for conflicting psychic forces.
items.cn: 1910 年心理学家布洛伊勒造 Ambivalenz，指相互冲突的心理力量。

items.en: ambivalent entered English through psychiatric writing, then spread to everyday use.
items.cn: ambivalent 借精神病学文献进入英语，随后扩展到日常用法。

items.en: Now the standard adjective for mixed feelings, in psychology and ordinary speech alike.
items.cn: 如今是表示「心情矛盾」的标准形容词，心理学与日常语通用。

note.en: Distinguish ambivalent from its sibling ambiguous and from near synonyms of hesitation.
note.cn: 要把 ambivalent 与同族词 ambiguous 区分开，也要与表示犹豫的近义词区分。

entries.definition: sharing ambi- but meaning unclear in meaning rather than mixed in feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 共享 ambi- 前缀，但指意义含混而非情感矛盾。

entries.definition: sharing ambi- and meaning able to use both hands equally well.
entries.definitionCN: 同前缀词，义为两手都能灵巧使用的。

entries.definition: the noun form: the state of having mixed feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词形式：矛盾心理的状态。

entries.definition: having opposing feelings, plainer and more colloquial than ambivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有对立情绪，比 ambivalent 更口语化。

entries.definition: open to two readings, stressing deliberate vagueness.
entries.definitionCN: 可作两种解读，强调有意含糊。

entries.definition: lacking full enthusiasm, a possible result of ambivalence.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏全部热情，可能是矛盾心理的结果。

normalIntro.en: Remember ambivalent through its two building blocks.
normalIntro.cn: 通过两个构件记住 ambivalent。

normal.en: ambi- (both) + valent (powers): two forces pulling at once.
normal.cn: ambi-（两边）+ valent（力量）：两股力量同时拉扯。

normal.en: Compare equivalent: same value; ambivalent: two values.
normal.cn: 对比 equivalent（同值）；ambivalent 则是两种价值并存。

normal.en: Think of an equal-arm balance holding love on one side, hate on the other.
normal.cn: 想想天平两端各放爱与恨，恰好平衡。

normal.en: Family chain: valere → valentia → ambivalent, from strong to capacity to two-way pull.
normal.cn: 词族链：valere → valentia → ambivalent，从强壮到能力到双向拉力。

normal.en: Feel ambivalent ABOUT something — the preposition almost always follows it.
normal.cn: 常用搭配是 feel ambivalent about something。

abstract.en: Picture two tiny people inside your chest pulling a rope in opposite directions.
abstract.cn: 想象胸中两个小人在朝相反方向拔河。

abstract.en: See one hand reaching out while the other pushes away.
abstract.cn: 看一只手伸出，另一只手推开。

abstract.en: Imagine a compass needle trembling between two magnets.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚指南针在两块磁铁之间颤抖不定。

examples.en: Many readers are ambivalent about the antihero.
examples.cn: 许多读者对这位反英雄态度矛盾。

examples.en: Her ambivalent smile gave nothing away.
examples.cn: 她那意味难辨的微笑不露声色。

examples.en: The city has long felt ambivalent about tourism.
examples.cn: 这座城市对旅游业的态度一直很矛盾。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安比瓦伦」——安比瓦伦站在天平中间，两边价值观各拉一头，左右为难。

root: 拉丁语 ambi-（两边）+ valere（强壮）派生的 valentia（力量），1910 年瑞士心理学家布洛伊勒据此造 Ambivalenz 表示「两种相互冲突的心理力量」，进入英语后为 ambivalent。同族词 equivalent（等值的）、ambidextrous（双手都灵巧的）。

sensesIntro.en: From two conflicting inner forces, the senses spread to hesitation between choices, contradictory signals, and mixed bonds to people, texts, and ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 从内心两种冲突力量出发，义项扩展到选项间的犹豫、矛盾的信号，以及对人、文本、观念的双重态度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two equal forces pulling a mind in opposite directions
core.cn: 核心意象：两股等量力量把心拉向两个方向

branches.en: Opposed emotions toward persons, things, or ideas.
branches.cn: 对人、事、观念的对立情感。

branches.en: Inability to choose between two options.
branches.cn: 在两个选项间难以抉择。

branches.en: Visible contradiction in words or behavior.
branches.cn: 言行上可见的自相矛盾。

branches.en: Psychological bonds carrying both attraction and aversion.
branches.cn: 兼具吸引与排斥的心理关系。

branches.en: Texts open to two conflicting interpretations.
branches.cn: 可作两种对立解读的文本。

intro.en: Ambivalent is built from a Latin prefix of duality and a root of strength.
intro.cn: ambivalent 由表示「双」的拉丁前缀和表示「力」的词根构成。

latinIntro.en: Both parts are pure Latin and remain transparent in modern English derivatives.
latinIntro.cn: 两个部分都是纯正拉丁语，在现代英语派生词中依然清晰可辨。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 中世纪哲学文献中的 valentia

definition_zh: 走动；行走；移动
definition_en: to walk or move from place to place, especially a formal or medical way of saying walk
core_image: 迈开双腿从一个地方挪到另一个地方
scene: 手术后护士鼓励病人下床练习。The patient was told to ambulate slowly along the corridor.
sceneCN: 这里的 ambulate 是「行走」（第 1 个义项：医学用语，指走动）；句意是护士让病人沿走廊慢慢走动。

pos.zh: 走动；行走（正式或医学用语）

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「行走；移动」
同族形容词，义为「能走动的；流动的；（建筑）回廊」
加前缀 circum- 构成，义为「绕行；绕……而走」
加前缀 per- 构成，义为「漫步；巡视」

senses.title: To walk, especially in medical contexts
senses.titleCN: 行走（医学用语）
senses.definition: to walk about, used formally or in hospitals for getting a patient moving
senses.definitionCN: 走动，正式用语或医院语境中指让病人下床活动
senses.example: Nurses helped him ambulate on the second day after surgery.
senses.exampleCN: 术后第二天护士搀扶他行走。
senses.why: Latin ambulare simply means to walk, and medicine keeps the learned verb for chart notes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ambulare 本义就是行走，医学在病历中保留了这一书面动词。

senses.title: To move about from place to place
senses.titleCN: 四处走动
senses.definition: to travel on foot from one location to another
senses.definitionCN: 步行从一个地点移动到另一个地点
senses.example: Visitors are free to ambulate through the sculpture garden.
senses.exampleCN: 参观者可在雕塑园内自由走动。
senses.why: The plain sense of walking extends to any movement on foot.
senses.whyCN: 行走的基本义可泛指一切步行移动。

senses.title: To regain the ability to walk
senses.titleCN: 恢复行走能力
senses.definition: to progress in rehabilitation until walking is possible again
senses.definitionCN: 在康复训练中逐步恢复行走功能
senses.example: After weeks of therapy she could ambulate without crutches.
senses.exampleCN: 经过数周治疗，她不用拐杖也能行走了。
senses.why: In rehabilitation the verb marks a milestone on the road back to walking.
senses.whyCN: 在康复语境中，这个动词标记通往恢复行走的里程碑。

senses.title: To walk as exercise or therapy
senses.titleCN: 行走锻炼或治疗
senses.definition: to walk deliberately for health or as part of treatment
senses.definitionCN: 为健康或作为治疗手段而进行的行走
senses.example: Cardiac patients are asked to ambulate for ten minutes each hour.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏病患者被要求每小时行走十分钟。
senses.why: When walking becomes a prescribed activity, the clinical verb fits the chart.
senses.whyCN: 当行走成为医嘱活动时，临床动词便与病历匹配。

senses.title: To move mechanically like walking
senses.titleCN: （机器）模拟行走
senses.definition: of a device or robot, to move in a walking manner
senses.definitionCN: 指装置或机器人以行走方式移动
senses.example: The rover ambulates over the simulated Martian soil.
senses.exampleCN: 探测器在模拟火星土壤上迈步行进。
senses.why: The learned verb is handy for machines whose legs imitate human walking.
senses.whyCN: 这一书面动词很适合描述用腿模仿人行走的机器。

senses.title: To pace or wander restlessly
senses.titleCN: 踱步；不安地走动
senses.definition: to walk up and down or wander, often from anxiety
senses.definitionCN: 来回踱步或游走，常因焦虑不安
senses.example: He ambulated the ward all night, unable to sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 他整晚在病房里踱步，无法入睡。
senses.why: Walking without a goal is still walking, and the verb covers restless pacing.
senses.whyCN: 没有目的的走动仍是行走，动词也涵盖不安的踱步。

intro.en: Ambulate comes straight from Latin ambulare, to walk, the same root behind ambulance and amble.
intro.cn: ambulate 直接来自拉丁语 ambulare（行走），与 ambulance、amble 同根。

items.en: A root meaning to go around, generally reconstructed for ambulare.
items.cn: 一般认为 ambulare 源自表示「四处走动」的重构词根。

items.en: ambulare, "to walk, go about".
items.cn: 拉丁语 ambulare「行走；四处走动」。

items.en: ambulare came to mean to fetch, as in fetching supplies by going about.
items.cn: 后期拉丁语中 ambulare 引申为「去取」，如外出取物。

items.en: the walking sense produced ambler, then hospital ambulante, a walking field hospital.
items.cn: 法语由行走义产生 ambler，另有医院 ambulante（流动战地医院）。

items.en: English ambulate appears in learned and medical prose in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 十七世纪英语 ambulate 出现于学术与医学散文。

items.en: Now chiefly a clinical and technical synonym for walk.
items.cn: 如今主要作为 walk 的临床和技术同义词。

note.en: Distinguish ambulate from its root family ambulare/amble/ambulance and from plain walk.
note.cn: 要把 ambulate 与词族 ambulare/amble/ambulance 区分开，也要与普通词 walk 区分。

entries.definition: same root adjective: able to walk; also a covered walkway in a church.
entries.definitionCN: 同根形容词：能走动的；也指教堂中的回廊。

entries.definition: same root: originally a moving field hospital, now an emergency vehicle.
entries.definitionCN: 同根词：原指流动战地医院，今指救护车。

entries.definition: same root through French: to walk at an easy, leisurely pace.
entries.definitionCN: 经法语同源：从容悠闲地走。

entries.definition: the everyday word; ambulate is its formal clinical twin.
entries.definitionCN: 日常用词；ambulate 是它的正式临床对应词。

entries.definition: to walk through or around, often for inspection.
entries.definitionCN: 步行穿过或巡视，常指查看。

entries.definition: to walk in a slow relaxed way.
entries.definitionCN: 悠闲缓步而行。

normalIntro.en: Remember ambulate through its root family of walking.
normalIntro.cn: 通过「行走」词族记住 ambulate。

normal.en: ambul- (walk) + -ate (verb): to walk.
normal.cn: ambul-（行走）+ -ate（动词后缀）：行走。

normal.en: An ambulance once 'walked' to the battlefield: a walking hospital.
normal.cn: ambulance 原是「走」向战场的流动医院。

normal.en: To amble is to walk lazily — same root, relaxed cousin.
normal.cn: amble 是懒洋洋地走——同根的悠闲亲戚。

normal.en: Hospitals love the word: ambulate the patient means get them walking.
normal.cn: 医院爱用这个词：ambulate the patient 即让病人下床走动。

normal.en: Family chain: ambulare → ambulatory → ambulate.
normal.cn: 词族链：ambulare → ambulatory → ambulate。

abstract.en: Picture a nurse holding a rolling pole beside a shuffling patient.
abstract.cn: 想象护士扶着输液架，陪病人缓缓挪步。

abstract.en: See footsteps printed one after another down a long corridor.
abstract.cn: 看长走廊上一串接一串的脚印。

abstract.en: Imagine a robot carefully placing one metal foot before the other.
abstract.cn: 想象机器人小心翼翼地交替迈出金属脚步。

examples.en: The surgeon wants the patient to ambulate twice a day.
examples.cn: 外科医生要求病人每天行走两次。

examples.en: Elderly residents ambulate in the garden every afternoon.
examples.cn: 老年住户每天下午在花园里散步。

examples.en: He slowly ambulated to the window for the first time in weeks.
examples.cn: 几周来他第一次慢慢走到了窗前。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不累特」——俺不累特能走，一天绕病房八圈。

root: 拉丁语 ambulare（行走；四处走动，一般认为源自表示「绕行」的重构词根）加英语动词后缀 -ate 构成 ambulate，字面义为「行走」。同族词有 ambulatory（可走动的）、ambulance（救护车，源自「流动医院」）、amble（缓行）。

sensesIntro.en: From plain walking, the senses extend to regaining the ability to walk, prescribed exercise, machine gaits, and restless pacing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从普通行走出发，义项扩展到恢复行走能力、医嘱锻炼、机器步态与不安踱步。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: legs carrying a body step by step down a corridor
core.cn: 核心意象：双腿一步一步把身体送过长廊

branches.en: Walking and moving about on foot.
branches.cn: 步行与四处走动。

branches.en: Recovering the ability to walk in rehabilitation.
branches.cn: 康复中恢复行走能力。

branches.en: Walking as ordered exercise or therapy.
branches.cn: 作为医嘱锻炼或治疗的行走。

branches.en: Robots and devices imitating the human walk.
branches.cn: 机器人与装置模仿人类步态。

branches.en: Restless wandering back and forth.
branches.cn: 不安的来回踱步。

intro.en: Ambulate is a Latin walking root with the common verb ending.
intro.cn: ambulate 由拉丁语行走词根加常见动词后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: The root ambulare stayed productive across French and English coinages.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ambulare 在法语和英语造词中一直保持能产性。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 古典拉丁语散文中的 ambulare

definition_zh: 伏击；埋伏；伏兵
definition_en: to hide and make a surprise attack on someone passing by; the act or place of such an attack
core_image: 草丛里屏住呼吸的士兵，等敌人一走进就猛扑上去
scene: 士兵们趴在高草深处一动不动地等待。The rebels planned to ambush the convoy at the narrow pass.
sceneCN: 这里的 ambush 是「伏击」（第 1 个义项：隐蔽突袭）；句意是叛军计划在狭窄山口伏击车队。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加名词后缀构成，义为「打埋伏的人；伏击者」
词根相关词，义为「灌木丛」，是 ambush 演变的线索之一

senses.title: To attack by surprise from concealment
senses.titleCN: 伏击：隐蔽处突袭
senses.definition: to hide and suddenly attack someone who is passing by
senses.definitionCN: 潜伏隐蔽，对经过者发动突然袭击
senses.example: Guerrillas ambushed the supply column at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 游击队员黎明时分伏击了补给纵队。
senses.why: The core image is waiting hidden in the bushes for the enemy to come close.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是藏在灌木丛中等敌人靠近。

senses.title: A surprise attack from hiding as a noun
senses.titleCN: 伏击（名词）
senses.definition: an act of attacking from a concealed position
senses.definitionCN: 从隐蔽位置发动的袭击
senses.example: Three soldiers died in the ambush.
senses.exampleCN: 三名士兵死于伏击。
senses.why: The verb names the action; the noun names the event itself.
senses.whyCN: 动词指动作，名词指这一事件本身。

senses.title: The place where attackers lie hidden
senses.titleCN: 埋伏地点
senses.definition: the concealed position chosen for a surprise attack
senses.definitionCN: 为突袭选择的隐蔽位置
senses.example: The scouts spotted the ambush by the broken bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 侦察兵在断桥边发现了埋伏。
senses.why: The hiding spot becomes the name of the whole waiting formation.
senses.whyCN: 藏身之处成为整个伏兵阵地的名称。

senses.title: A surprise verbal or social attack
senses.titleCN: （言语、社交上的）突然袭击
senses.definition: an unexpected confrontation or tricky question posed without warning
senses.definitionCN: 毫无预警的突然质问或围攻
senses.example: Reporters laid an ambush of hard questions at the press conference.
senses.exampleCN: 记者们在发布会上用尖锐问题设下埋伏。
senses.why: Being caught unprepared is shared by both battlefield and interview room.
senses.whyCN: 战场与访谈间的共性是「措手不及」。

senses.title: To waylay someone for an unexpected meeting
senses.titleCN: （非敌意）突然拦截
senses.definition: to intercept someone unexpectedly, sometimes in fun or for a surprise
senses.definitionCN: 出其不意地拦住某人，有时是玩笑或惊喜
senses.example: His teammates ambushed him with a birthday cake.
senses.exampleCN: 队友们捧着生日蛋糕给了他一个惊喜突袭。
senses.why: The surprise element alone survives when hostility drops away.
senses.whyCN: 当敌意消失后，只剩下「出其不意」这一要素。

senses.title: Hidden danger awaiting the unwary
senses.titleCN: 潜伏的危险
senses.definition: a concealed threat or trap awaiting the careless
senses.definitionCN: 潜伏在暗处等待大意者的危险或陷阱
senses.example: Debt lay in ambush behind every easy loan offer.
senses.exampleCN: 每笔轻松贷款的背后都潜伏着债务陷阱。
senses.why: The hidden-waiting image transfers to any unseen peril.
senses.whyCN: 「暗中等待」的意象转移到任何看不见的危险。

intro.en: Ambush comes through Old French embusche from a Frankish word meaning to place in a wood, literally to hide in the bushes.
intro.cn: ambush 经古法语 embusche 源自法兰克语词，义为「藏进林中」，字面即「藏进灌木丛」。

items.en: bosk or busk, "bush, wood", the source root, generally reconstructed.
items.cn: 法兰克语 bosk/busk「灌木、树林」，为词根来源（一般认为）。

items.en: embuschier, "to place in the woods, lay an ambush"; embusche, the ambush itself.
items.cn: 古法语 embuschier「置于林中、设伏」；embusche 指伏击。

items.en: embush / ambush entered English with medieval warfare vocabulary.
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语 embush/ambush 随中世纪战争词汇进入英语。

items.en: English ambush appears in the thirteenth to fourteenth century.
items.cn: 十三至十四世纪英语 ambush 出现。

items.en: Now standard for surprise attacks in war, sport, and metaphor.
items.cn: 如今是战争、竞技及隐喻中「突袭」的标准词。

note.en: Distinguish ambush from the plain noun bush and from near synonyms of surprise attack.
note.cn: 要把 ambush 与普通名词 bush 区分开，也要与表示突袭的近义词区分。

entries.definition: the simple noun for a shrub, holding the original 'woods' image inside ambush.
entries.definitionCN: 灌木的普通名词，ambush 里藏着的正是「树丛」这一原初意象。

entries.definition: a unit of measure, from French boissel; only looks related.
entries.definitionCN: 计量单位，源自法语 boissel，仅形近。

entries.definition: to raise a design on a surface; shares the em-/am- prefix shape only.
entries.definitionCN: 指在表面压出浮雕，仅前缀形状相似，词源无关。

entries.definition: to wait for and stop someone on their way.
entries.definitionCN: 在路上等候拦截某人。

entries.definition: to catch by a concealed device or scheme.
entries.definitionCN: 用暗设装置或圈套捕获。

entries.definition: a direct violent attack, without the hiding element.
entries.definitionCN: 正面强攻，不含隐蔽要素。

normalIntro.en: Remember ambush through its bush root.
normalIntro.cn: 通过词根 bush 记住 ambush。

normal.en: am- (in) + bush: hiding in the bushes.
normal.cn: am-（进入）+ bush（灌木丛）：藏进树丛。

normal.en: See the word bush inside ambush — the hiding place itself.
normal.cn: ambush 里看得见 bush——藏身处本身。

normal.en: Compare emboss: em-/am- often means 'put into'.
normal.cn: 对比 emboss：em-/am- 常表「放入」。

normal.en: Common frames: lay an ambush, spring an ambush, walk into an ambush.
normal.cn: 常见搭配：lay an ambush、spring an ambush、walk into an ambush。

normal.en: Family chain: bush → embuschier → ambush, from shrub to hiding to attack.
normal.cn: 词族链：bush → embuschier → ambush，从树丛到藏匿到袭击。

abstract.en: Picture eyes blinking behind tall grass as boots pass by.
abstract.cn: 想象深草后眨动的眼睛，看着军靴走过。

abstract.en: Hear the sudden crackle as the hidden men leap up.
abstract.cn: 听潜伏者跃起时草丛的骤响。

abstract.en: Imagine a cake bursting from behind a door instead of bullets.
abstract.cn: 想象门后跳出的不是子弹而是蛋糕。

examples.en: The patrol walked straight into an ambush.
examples.cn: 巡逻队径直走进了埋伏。

examples.en: They ambushed the runners at the forest trail.
examples.cn: 他们在林间小径伏击了那群跑者。

examples.en: Interviewers set an ambush of tricky questions.
examples.cn: 采访者设下一连串刁钻问题的埋伏。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不输」——俺埋伏得好俺不输，等敌人进了圈套再动手。

root: 一般认为源自日耳曼语（法兰克语）bosc/busk「灌木、树林」，经古法语 embuschier「藏进林中、设伏」与 embusche（伏击）进入英语，为 ambush，字面义为「藏进树丛（攻击）」。英语 bush（灌木）是同源词。

sensesIntro.en: From hiding in the bushes to attack, the senses spread to the attack itself, its location, verbal traps, playful surprises, and hidden danger.
sensesIntro.cn: 从藏进树丛发起攻击出发，义项扩展到袭击事件、伏击地点、言语圈套、善意惊喜与潜伏的危险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: attackers hidden in the bushes waiting for their prey
core.cn: 核心意象：袭击者藏于树丛中等候猎物

branches.en: The surprise attack from a hidden position.
branches.cn: 自隐蔽位置发动的突袭。

branches.en: The attack as an event and as a chosen place.
branches.cn: 作为事件与地点的伏击。

branches.en: Unwarned hostile questioning or confrontation.
branches.cn: 毫无预警的敌意质问或对峙。

branches.en: Playful or friendly surprise interception.
branches.cn: 玩笑式或友好的惊喜拦截。

branches.en: Any concealed peril awaiting the careless.
branches.cn: 等待大意者的任何潜伏危险。

intro.en: Ambush preserves an old 'put into the woods' formation.
intro.cn: ambush 保留了古老的「置于林中」构词。

latinIntro.en: Though now spelled am-, the prefix matches French em-, itself from Latin in-.
latinIntro.cn: 如今拼作 am- 的前缀对应法语 em-，其源头是拉丁语 in-。

items.meaning: to lie in wait on the way

items.exampleCN: 见莎士比亚作品中的 embosked

definition_zh: 芬芳甘美的；美味可口得像神食的；令人愉悦至极的
definition_en: deliciously fragrant or tasty, worthy of the gods; extremely pleasing
core_image: 众神餐桌上的甘露美食：香气扑鼻、凡人尝一口便忘不掉
scene: 烘焙房刚出炉的面包香气飘满整条街，路人纷纷驻足。The kitchen filled with an ambrosial smell of honey and warm bread.
sceneCN: 这里的 ambrosial 是「芬芳甘美的」（第 1 个义项：气味甜美如神食）；句意是厨房里弥漫着蜂蜜和热面包的芬芳香气。

pos.zh: 芬芳甘美的；美味如神食的

derivatives.zh: 由名词 ambrosia 加形容词后缀 -al 构成的基础词，义为「神的食物；甘露；美味佳肴」
形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「芬芳甘美地」

senses.title: Deliciously fragrant or flavorful
senses.titleCN: 芬芳甘美的：气味或滋味甜美
senses.definition: having an extremely pleasing smell or taste, as if fit for the gods
senses.definitionCN: 气味或滋味极其宜人，仿佛只有神才配享用
senses.example: The ambrosial perfume of jasmine drifted through the open window.
senses.exampleCN: 茉莉花的芬芳从敞开的窗口飘进来。
senses.why: The word descends from ambrosia, the food of the Greek gods, so anything heavenly in smell or taste earns this adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源自希腊神话中众神的食物 ambrosia，凡是香气或滋味达到「神级」的东西就配得上这个形容词。

senses.title: Worthy of or relating to the food of the gods
senses.titleCN: 神食般的：与诸神食物相关
senses.definition: of or relating to ambrosia, the mythical food of the Greek gods
senses.definitionCN: 与希腊神话中众神食物 ambrosia 有关的
senses.example: Ancient poets described ambrosial banquets on Mount Olympus.
senses.exampleCN: 古代诗人描绘过奥林匹斯山上的神食盛宴。
senses.why: The direct adjectival form keeps the original mythological reference before extending to everyday delight.
senses.whyCN: 形容词本义直接保留神话指涉，之后才延伸到日常的愉悦体验。

senses.title: Extremely pleasing or delightful in general
senses.titleCN: 令人愉悦至极的：泛指极致享受
senses.definition: giving intense pleasure or delight beyond food and smell
senses.definitionCN: 在饮食气味之外给予强烈愉悦感的
senses.example: They spent an ambrosial afternoon doing nothing by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在湖边度过了一个惬意至极、无所事事的下午。
senses.why: Once something is 'good enough for the gods', the sense widens to any experience of pure bliss.
senses.whyCN: 既然达到了「配得上众神」的程度，词义就顺理成章地扩展到任何纯粹的幸福体验。

senses.title: Divinely sweet in literary description
senses.titleCN: 文学中的甘美描绘
senses.definition: used in poetry and literature to describe sweetness with a divine or elevated tone
senses.definitionCN: 诗歌文学中以神圣或高雅口吻描写甘美的用语
senses.example: The poet called her voice ambrosial music.
senses.exampleCN: 诗人称她的嗓音为甘美如神乐的音乐。
senses.why: Writers borrow the mythic register to raise ordinary sweetness into something sacred.
senses.whyCN: 作家借用神话语域，把平凡的甘甜提升到神圣的高度。

senses.title: Immortality-conferring in classical myth
senses.titleCN: 古典神话中赐予不朽的
senses.definition: describing the quality of ambrosia that granted immortality to the gods
senses.definitionCN: 形容神话中神食赋予众神不朽的那种性质
senses.example: Legend held that ambrosial nectar kept the gods forever young.
senses.exampleCN: 传说甘美的神酒让众神永葆青春。
senses.why: Because ambrosia literally meant 'immortality' in Greek, the adjective can carry that life-giving force.
senses.whyCN: ambrosia 在希腊语中字面意思就是「不朽」，因此形容词也能带有赐予生命力的含义。

senses.title: Delicately sweet in describing nature
senses.titleCN: 描绘自然的清甜
senses.definition: describing the gentle sweetness of natural air, weather, or surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 形容自然空气、天气或环境的柔和清甜
senses.example: An ambrosial breeze came off the orange groves.
senses.exampleCN: 一阵清甜的微风从橙树林那边吹来。
senses.why: Nature writing stretches the food metaphor to the air itself, as if breathing were tasting.
senses.whyCN: 自然文学把食物的比喻延伸到空气本身，仿佛呼吸也是在品尝。

intro.en: Ambrosial is the adjective of ambrosia, the legendary food of the Greek gods, from a root meaning 'immortal'.
intro.cn: ambrosial 是 ambrosia（希腊神话中众神的食物）的形容词，词根意为「不朽的」。

items.en: Root *mer-, 'to rub away, die', also seen in mortal.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *mer-「消逝、死亡」，也见于 mortal（凡人）。

items.en: ambrosia, literally 'immortality', from a- (not) plus brotos (mortal), the divine food and also an ointment.
items.cn: 希腊语 ambrosia，字面义「不朽」，由 a-（不）+ brotos（会死的）构成，指神的食物与膏油。

items.en: ambrosia borrowed directly from Greek in classical texts.
items.cn: 拉丁语在古典文献中直接借入 ambrosia。

items.en: English ambrosia appears in translations of classical myth.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 ambrosia 随古典神话译作进入英语。

items.en: Writers formed ambrosial with the adjectival suffix -al to describe anything godlike in sweetness.
items.cn: 十七、十八世纪作家加形容词后缀 -al 造出 ambrosial，形容一切甜美如神赐的事物。

items.en: Now used for deliciously fragrant food and intensely pleasant experiences.
items.cn: 如今用于形容芬芳美味的食物以及极其愉悦的体验。

note.en: Keep ambrosial apart from its noun ambrosia and from near-synonyms of sweetness and fragrance.
note.cn: 要把 ambrosial 与其名词 ambrosia 区分开，也要与表示甜美芬芳的近义词区分。

entries.definition: the food of the Greek gods; any delicious food or dessert.
entries.definitionCN: 希腊众神的食物；泛指美味食物或甜品，是 ambrosial 的名词基础。

entries.definition: a house of prostitution; shares no root with ambrosial, only loose spelling overlap.
entries.definitionCN: 妓院；与 ambrosial 词源毫无关系，仅拼写略显相近。

entries.definition: cruel and violent; from Latin brutus, unrelated in meaning despite similar -al ending.
entries.definitionCN: 残忍粗暴的；源自拉丁语 brutus，意义与 ambrosial 截然相反，仅后缀形似。

entries.definition: sweet as nectar; the sister adjective built on the gods' drink.
entries.definitionCN: 如神饮般甘甜的，由众神饮品 nectar 构成的姊妹形容词。

entries.definition: highly pleasant to taste or smell, in everyday register.
entries.definitionCN: 美味的、好闻的，日常语域中最常用的说法。

entries.definition: having a pleasant smell, without the divine connotation.
entries.definitionCN: 芬芳的，只说好闻，不带神圣色彩。

normalIntro.en: Break ambrosial into its immortal pieces.
normalIntro.cn: 把 ambrosial 拆成「不朽」的构件来记。

normal.en: ambrosia + -al: the adjective of the gods' food.
normal.cn: ambrosia（神食）+ -al（形容词后缀）：众神美食的形容词。

normal.en: a- (not) + brotos (mortal): literally 'not dying' — food that makes you immortal.
normal.cn: a-（不）+ brotos（会死的）：字面即「不死」——吃了能长生。

normal.en: Family chain: immortal → ambrosia → ambrosial, from 'undying' to 'divinely delicious'.
normal.cn: 词族链：immortal（不朽的）→ ambrosia（神食）→ ambrosial（甘美如神食的）。

normal.en: Cousin word: nectar for the gods' drink, ambrosia for their food.
normal.cn: 亲戚词：nectar 是众神的饮品，ambrosia 是众神的餐食。

normal.en: Same -al pattern: region → regional, ambrosia → ambrosial.
normal.cn: 同样的 -al 构词：region → regional，ambrosia → ambrosial。

abstract.en: Picture a golden plate floating down from Olympus; the smell alone makes you feel immortal.
abstract.cn: 想象奥林匹斯山上飘下一只金盘，光闻香气就仿佛长生不老。

abstract.en: Say 'am-BRO-zhal' and hear 'am NOT broken' — divine food never spoils.
abstract.cn: 读 am-BRO-zhal 时联想「不会坏」——神食永不腐坏。

abstract.en: One bite of ambrosial cake and the whole street stops to breathe it in.
abstract.cn: 咬一口甘美如神食的蛋糕，整条街的人都停下来深吸香气。

examples.en: The ambrosial scent of ripe mangoes filled the market.
examples.cn: 熟芒果的芬芳弥漫了整个市场。

examples.en: Grandmother's ambrosial apple pie vanished within minutes.
examples.cn: 祖母做的甘美苹果派几分钟就被吃光了。

examples.en: Nothing at the feast was more ambrosial than the honeyed wine.
examples.cn: 宴席上没有比蜂蜜酒更甘美的东西了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不臭哟」——俺做的菜芬芳甘美，一点都不臭，香得像神仙吃的。

root: 希腊语 a-（不）+ brotos（会死的，与拉丁 mort- 同源于印欧词根 *mer-「死亡」），ambrosia 即「不朽之物」，指众神的食物；加形容词后缀 -al 得 ambrosial，即「神食般的甘美」。

sensesIntro.en: From the literal food of the gods, ambrosial spreads to any divinely sweet smell, taste, or pleasure.
sensesIntro.cn: 从字面的「众神食物」出发，ambrosial 扩展到一切甘美神圣的气味、滋味与愉悦体验。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the immortal food of the gods
core.cn: 核心意象：让众神不朽的甘美食物

branches.en: Pleasant smells and flavors of food and nature
branches.cn: 食物与自然的芬芳甘美

branches.en: Direct reference to the mythic banquet of Olympus
branches.cn: 直接指涉奥林匹斯的神话盛宴

branches.en: Any experience of supreme delight
branches.cn: 任何极致愉悦的体验

branches.en: Elevated literary style for sweetness
branches.cn: 文学化的甘美修辞

branches.en: The life-giving, death-defying force of the divine food
branches.cn: 神食赐予生命、抗拒死亡的力量

intro.en: Ambrosial shows the Greek negative prefix a- plus a root of dying, sealed with the Latin-style adjective suffix -al.
intro.cn: ambrosial 体现希腊语否定前缀 a- 加「死亡」词根，再配拉丁风格形容词后缀 -al 的构词。

latinIntro.en: The same roots appear in Latin borrowings about life, death, and sweetness.
latinIntro.cn: 同样的词根也出现在关于生死与甘甜的拉丁借词中。

items.exampleCN: nature（自然）加 -al 变成 natural（自然的）

items.meaning: the state of being mortal; death rate

items.example: the body was taken to the mortuary

items.meaning: the drink of the gods; sweet liquid of flowers
a smooth-skinned peach, named for its sweetness
items.example: she sliced a nectarine for breakfast
items.exampleCN: 她切了一个油桃当早餐

items.meaningCN: 谋杀；与「死亡」词根同源的日耳曼同族词

definition_zh: 愿意服从的；顺从的；经得起检验的；有义务服从的
definition_en: willing to agree, cooperate, or submit to authority; open to testing or control
core_image: 温和低头的人：别人一提建议就点头配合
scene: 新来的实习生脾气很好，什么安排都乐意接受。The new intern was amenable to every suggestion the manager made.
sceneCN: 这里的 amenable 是「愿意服从的、通情达理的」（第 1 个义项：乐于接受建议）；句意是这位新实习生对经理的每个建议都很乐意配合。

pos.zh: 愿服从的；通情达理的；肯合作的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「顺从地；乐于配合地」
形容词加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「顺从性；可支配性」

senses.title: Willing to cooperate or agree
senses.titleCN: 愿意配合的：乐于点头答应
senses.definition: open and responsive to suggestion; willing to agree or cooperate
senses.definitionCN: 对建议持开放态度，愿意同意或配合
senses.example: The landlord proved amenable to lowering the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东愿意配合降低租金。
senses.why: The Latin root minare means to drive animals with threats; a tame animal is one you can lead, hence a person you can persuade.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 minare 意为「驱赶牲畜」，温驯的牲畜可以牵走，由此引申为可以被说服的人。

senses.title: Responsible to a legal authority
senses.titleCN: 法律上须服从的：受管辖
senses.definition: liable to be brought under the jurisdiction or authority of a court or law
senses.definitionCN: 应受法院或法律管辖的，负服从义务的
senses.example: Foreign diplomats are amenable to local traffic laws in most countries.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数国家，外交官也须遵守当地交通法规。
senses.why: If a person can be 'led' by the law, the same herding image becomes legal obligation.
senses.whyCN: 既然一个人能被法律「牵引」，驱赶牲畜的意象就变成了法律义务。

senses.title: Open to testing or analysis
senses.titleCN: 经得起检验的：可供研究处理
senses.definition: capable of being tested, analyzed, or dealt with by a method
senses.definitionCN: 能够用某种方法加以检验、分析或处理的
senses.example: The data were amenable to statistical analysis.
senses.exampleCN: 这些数据适合做统计分析。
senses.why: What willingly yields to a person also yields to a procedure; the word transfers to things.
senses.whyCN: 乐于向人让步的东西同样乐于向方法让步，词义由此转移到事物上。

senses.title: Responsive to medical treatment
senses.titleCN: 对治疗有反应的
senses.definition: responding favorably to medical treatment or therapy
senses.definitionCN: 对医疗或治疗产生良好反应的
senses.example: This cancer is highly amenable to radiation therapy.
senses.exampleCN: 这种癌症对放射治疗反应良好。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the sense of yielding: a disease that 'obeys' treatment is amenable.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用了「顺服」之义：肯「听话」的疾病就是对治疗有反应的疾病。

senses.title: Easily guided in temperament
senses.titleCN: 性情温顺易引导的
senses.definition: having a mild, tractable disposition that others can guide
senses.definitionCN: 性情温和、容易被他人引导的
senses.example: Puppies that are amenable are much easier to train.
senses.exampleCN: 性情温顺的幼犬训练起来容易得多。
senses.why: The original image of driving livestock stays closest to the surface when we describe an animal's temperament.
senses.whyCN: 描述动物性情时，「驱赶牲畜」的本源意象最为贴近字面。

senses.title: Subject to rules or conditions
senses.titleCN: 受规则条件约束的
senses.definition: subject or subordinate to rules, conditions, or procedures
senses.definitionCN: 受规则、条件或程序约束的
senses.example: Membership benefits are amenable to the club's regulations.
senses.exampleCN: 会员权益须遵守俱乐部章程。
senses.why: Anything placed under a system is, figuratively, being led along that system's track.
senses.whyCN: 凡被纳入某个体系的事物，形象地说都是沿着该体系的轨道被牵引前行。

intro.en: Amenable traces to Anglo-French and medieval Latin words about leading animals, ultimately a metaphor for being led.
intro.cn: amenable 源自盎格鲁-法语和中世纪拉丁语中「驱赶牲畜」的词，最终是「被牵引」的隐喻。

items.en: Root *mei-, to move or drive, source of Latin minare.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *mei-「移动、驱赶」，是拉丁语 minare 的来源。

items.en: minare, to drive animals with cries or threats; minari, to threaten.
items.cn: 拉丁语 minare「以呼喝驱赶牲畜」；minari「威吓」。

items.en: aminare, to lead by threats; adjective aminabilis, liable to be led.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 aminare「以威吓牵引」，形容词 aminabilis「可被牵引的」。

items.en: amener, to lead or bring, from a- (to) plus mener (to lead).
items.cn: 盎格鲁-法语 amener「引领、带来」，由 a-（向）+ mener（引导）构成。

items.en: English amenable first meant liable to be brought to account, then willing to be led.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语 amenable 先指「应被追究责任」，后转为「愿意被引导」。

items.en: Now chiefly an agreeable, cooperative temperament or openness to treatment and analysis.
items.cn: 如今主要表示性格随和配合，或对治疗、分析持开放态度。

note.en: Do not confuse amenable with amendable or amenity; and pick near-synonyms carefully by register.
note.cn: 不要把 amenable 与 amendable、amenity 混淆；近义词也要按语域仔细区分。

entries.definition: able to be corrected or changed; from Latin emendare, not from minare.
entries.definitionCN: 可修正的、可修改的；源自拉丁语 emendare，与 amenable 词根不同，仅形近。

entries.definition: a pleasant feature or convenience; shares spelling start but a different branch of meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 便利设施、宜人之处；拼写开头相似但词义分支不同，注意区分。

entries.definition: friendly and pleasant in manner; from Latin amare, to love — a different root despite similar sound.
entries.definitionCN: 和蔼可亲的；源自拉丁语 amare「爱」，词根不同但读音相近，易混。

entries.definition: obeying rules or requests, sometimes with a hint of passivity.
entries.definitionCN: 顺从的、依从的，有时略带被动意味。

entries.definition: easily controlled or managed, like docile animals or solvable problems.
entries.definitionCN: 易驾驭的、易处理的，既可指温驯也可指问题易解。

entries.definition: willing to receive new ideas or suggestions.
entries.definitionCN: 乐于接受新想法或建议的。

normalIntro.en: Link amenable to being led without resistance.
normalIntro.cn: 把 amenable 联想为「不抵抗地被牵引」。

normal.en: a- (to) + men- (drive, lead): one who is led easily.
normal.cn: a-（向）+ men-（驱赶、引导）：容易被牵引的人。

normal.en: Same men- family: amenable, menace (threat used to drive), amenable to reason.
normal.cn: men- 词族：amenable（顺从的）、menace（用于驱赶的威吓）、服理。

normal.en: Picture a farmer leading a calm ox — amenable to the rope.
normal.cn: 想象农夫牵着一头安静的牛——对缰绳十分顺从。

normal.en: Common pattern: amenable to + noun (change, reason, treatment).
normal.cn: 常见搭配：amenable to + 名词（改变、道理、治疗）。

normal.en: Contrast: amendable = can be fixed; amenable = willing to follow.
normal.cn: 对比：amendable 是「可修改」，amenable 是「愿意服从」。

abstract.en: Imagine a door with no lock: it opens amenable to every knock.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇没上锁的门：谁来敲都乐意开，即「顺从配合」。

abstract.en: See a meeting where everyone nods; the whole room is amenable.
abstract.cn: 想象会议室里人人点头，全场都「乐于配合」。

abstract.en: Think of soft clay: amenable to every shape the sculptor wants.
abstract.cn: 想想柔软的陶泥：任凭雕塑家摆弄，即「易处理、顺从」。

examples.en: She is amenable to working weekends if the deadline requires it.
examples.cn: 如果截止日期需要，她愿意周末加班。

examples.en: The dispute was finally resolved because both sides were amenable to mediation.
examples.cn: 双方都愿意接受调解，争端最终得到解决。

examples.en: Early-stage illness is far more amenable to treatment.
examples.cn: 早期疾病对治疗的反应要好得多。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿妹闹不」——阿妹一点也不闹，别人说什么都是「不闹、都行」，特别顺从好说话。

root: 一般认为源自拉丁语 minare（驱赶牲畜）→ 中世纪拉丁语 aminabilis（可被牵引的）→ 盎格鲁-法语 amener（带来），进入英语后由「应被追究」转为「愿意被引导」，词根属「牵引」意象，词源链条中段存在重构成分。

sensesIntro.en: From the image of a tractable animal being led, amenable extends to legal obedience, workable data, and treatable illness.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「温驯牲畜被牵引」的意象出发，amenable 扩展到法律服从、数据可分析、疾病可治疗等用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calm animal that lets itself be led
core.cn: 核心意象：甘愿被牵引的温驯牲畜

branches.en: Agreeable temperament, in people and animals
branches.cn: 人与动物温顺配合的性情

branches.en: Falling under legal or institutional authority
branches.cn: 受法律或机构权威管辖

branches.en: Problems and data that yield to analysis
branches.cn: 可被分析方法处理的问题与数据

branches.en: Diseases that respond to therapy
branches.cn: 对治疗有反应的疾病

branches.en: Things bound by rules and conditions
branches.cn: 受规则条件约束的事物

intro.en: Amenable combines a prefix of direction, a root of driving, and an adjective suffix of capability.
intro.cn: amensible 由方向前缀、「驱赶」词根和表示能力的形容词后缀组合而成。

latinIntro.en: The root family spreads through words of threat and leading.
latinIntro.cn: 该词族散布于表示威吓与引导的词汇中。

items.exampleCN: 酒后驾车的司机是威胁

items.exampleCN: 和蔼的主人迎接了我们

items.example: the contract is amendable by both parties

definition_zh: 修改；修正；改良；改正（行为）
definition_en: to change or improve something, especially a text or law; to reform one's ways
core_image: 拿起笔把错处涂掉补上：文件修好，人也改好
scene: 委员会讨论后决定对章程中过时的条款动笔修改。The committee voted to amend the outdated section of the constitution.
sceneCN: 这里的 amend 是「修改、修正」（第 1 个义项：对条文正式修改）；句意是委员会投票决定修改宪法中过时的条款。

derivatives.zh: 动词加名词后缀 -ment 构成，义为「修正案；修改」
动词加形容词后缀 -able 构成，义为「可修正的」
动词加施动者后缀 -er 构成，义为「修改者」
同源词，经拉丁语 emendare 进入英语，义为「校勘改正（文本）」

senses.title: To make formal changes to a text or law
senses.titleCN: 修改条文：对文本或法律作正式修改
senses.definition: to alter formally, especially a legal document or proposed legislation
senses.definitionCN: 对文本尤其是法律文件作正式修改
senses.example: Parliament moved to amend the voting law before the election.
senses.exampleCN: 议会着手在选举前修改选举法。
senses.why: The Latin root mendare means to free from fault; a formal edit strips errors from a text.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 mendare 意为「除去缺陷」，正式修订就是把文本中的错误清除。

senses.title: To correct a small fault or improve something
senses.titleCN: 修正改良：改正小毛病、加以改进
senses.definition: to put right a minor error or make something slightly better
senses.definitionCN: 改正小错误或使某物略有改进
senses.example: She amended her essay after the teacher's comments.
senses.exampleCN: 根据老师的评语，她修改了作文。
senses.why: Beyond laws, any writing or plan can be freed from its small defects.
senses.whyCN: 除法律外，任何文字或计划都可以被清除小缺陷，词义随之泛化。

senses.title: To reform one's own behavior
senses.titleCN: 改过自新：改正自身行为
senses.definition: to change one's conduct for the better; to give up bad habits
senses.definitionCN: 使自身行为变好，改掉坏习惯
senses.example: After the scandal, he vowed to amend his ways.
senses.exampleCN: 丑闻之后，他发誓改过自新。
senses.why: The cleansing image turns inward: a person, like a text, can be edited free of faults.
senses.whyCN: 净化的意象转向人自身：人如文本，也能被修改掉缺陷。

senses.title: To make amends by compensation
senses.titleCN: 补偿弥补：以行动弥补过错
senses.definition: to repair a wrong by paying or doing something in return
senses.definitionCN: 通过赔偿或行动来弥补过错
senses.example: He worked weekends to make amends for missing the deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 他周末加班，以弥补误了截止日期的过失。
senses.why: Fixing a fault extends to fixing the harm a fault caused, which requires repayment.
senses.whyCN: 「修复缺陷」延伸到「修复缺陷造成的伤害」，后者就需要补偿。

senses.title: To improve soil or growing conditions
senses.titleCN: 改良土壤
senses.definition: to improve the quality of soil by adding material to it
senses.definitionCN: 通过添加物料改善土壤质量
senses.example: Gardeners amend heavy clay soil with compost.
senses.exampleCN: 园丁用堆肥改良黏重的土壤。
senses.why: Gardening treats the earth as a document with faults that can be corrected by additives.
senses.whyCN: 园艺把土地看作有缺陷的文本，可以通过添加物料来「修改」。

senses.title: To edit a scholarly text
senses.titleCN: 校勘文本：学术性订正
senses.definition: to correct a text critically, as in editing an old manuscript
senses.definitionCN: 以校勘方式订正文本，如整理古代抄本
senses.example: Scholars amended the corrupted passages of the manuscript.
senses.exampleCN: 学者们订正了抄本中讹误的段落。
senses.why: This is the oldest scholarly use, close to the twin word emend, both meaning fault-removal.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的学术用法，与孪生词 emend 同出「除错」之义。

intro.en: Amend descends from Latin emendare, 'to free from fault', built on the root menda, a defect.
intro.cn: amend 源自拉丁语 emendare「使免于缺陷」，词根 menda 意为「缺陷」。

items.en: Root *mend-, physical defect or fault, also seen in mendacity.
items.cn: 原始印欧语词根 *mend-「身体缺陷、过错」，也见于 mendacity（撒谎）。

items.en: menda, a fault or blemish; emendare, to correct by removing faults.
items.cn: 拉丁语 menda「缺陷、污点」；emendare「除错改正」。

items.en: amender, to correct or repair, from a- (to) plus amender root.
items.cn: 古法语 amender「改正、修复」，由 a-（向）加词根构成。

items.en: English amend appears meaning to repair or free from fault.
items.cn: 十三世纪英语 amend 出现，意为修复、去除缺陷。

items.en: The legal sense of amending statutes and constitutions became central.
items.cn: 十七、十八世纪修订法律与宪法的用法成为核心义项。

items.en: Now used for legal edits, small corrections, personal reform, and soil improvement.
items.cn: 如今用于法律修订、小修正、个人改过以及改良土壤。

note.en: Watch the near-twins amend, emend, and mend, plus rival verbs for changing texts.
note.cn: 注意 amend、emend、mend 这组近似词，以及修改文本的其他动词。

entries.definition: to correct a text critically; the pure Latin form for scholarly editing.
entries.definitionCN: 校勘订正文本；纯拉丁形式的学术用语，与 amend 同根。

entries.definition: a shortened form of amend, meaning to repair things or improve situations.
entries.definitionCN: amend 的缩略形式，指修补物件或改善状况。

entries.definition: capable of being amended or corrected.
entries.definitionCN: 可修正的、可修改的，amend 的形容词形式。

entries.definition: to re-examine and change, often broadly rather than in small patches.
entries.definitionCN: 修订、修改，往往是大范围重看重改。

entries.definition: to set something wrong right, formal register.
entries.definitionCN: 纠正、矫正，语域正式。

entries.definition: to change partially, without the moral tone of fault-removal.
entries.definitionCN: 局部修改，不含「除错改过」的道德色彩。

normalIntro.en: Anchor amend on the idea of removing a fault.
normalIntro.cn: 把 amend 锚定在「去除缺陷」这个核心上。

normal.en: a- + mend: mend (repair) with a prefix — amend, then shorten back to mend.
normal.cn: a- + mend：先加前缀成 amend（修正），再缩略回 mend（修补）。

normal.en: Latin menda = fault; emendare = drive the fault out.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 menda 即「缺陷」，emendare 即「把缺陷赶出去」。

normal.en: Family chain: menda → emend → amend → amendment.
normal.cn: 词族链：menda（缺陷）→ emend（校勘）→ amend（修正）→ amendment（修正案）。

normal.en: Remember the Five Amendments of the US Bill of Rights pattern: amend the constitution.
normal.cn: 联想美国权利法案的修正案传统：amend the constitution。

normal.en: make amends = make the fault whole again.
normal.cn: make amends 即「把过错弥补完整」。

abstract.en: See a red pen circling a flaw in the law and writing a better line beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象红笔圈出法条瑕疵，在旁边写下更好的表述。

abstract.en: Picture kneading dough: press out the lump, and the dough is amended.
abstract.cn: 想象揉面团：把疙瘩揉开，面团就「修正」好了。

abstract.en: A person saying sorry plus coffee for a broken mug — that is amends.
abstract.cn: 打碎杯子后道歉再请喝咖啡——这就是「弥补」。

examples.en: The board agreed to amend the bylaws at the next meeting.
examples.cn: 董事会同意在下次会议上修改章程。

examples.en: He apologized and promised to amend his behavior.
examples.cn: 他道了歉，并保证改正自己的行为。

examples.en: To make amends, the airline upgraded every affected passenger.
examples.cn: 为了弥补过失，航空公司为所有受影响的乘客升了舱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿门德」——念句「阿门」忏悔自己的错误，然后动手修改改正，改完心安。

root: 源自拉丁语 emendare「去除缺陷」，由 ex-（出）+ menda（缺陷、污点）构成；经古法语 amender 进入英语。同根词 emend（校勘）、mend（修补）、mendacity（说谎，含「缺陷」引申义）。

sensesIntro.en: Starting from fault-removal in texts, amend spreads to laws, personal reform, compensation, and even garden soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「清除文本缺陷」出发，amend 扩展到法律修订、个人改过、过错补偿乃至改良土壤。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: pressing out a flaw until the surface is clean
core.cn: 核心意象：把缺陷压出去，让表面恢复干净

branches.en: Statutes and constitutions formally edited
branches.cn: 法律与宪法的正式修订

branches.en: Small corrections and scholarly editing of texts
branches.cn: 小处修正与文本校勘

branches.en: A person editing out bad habits
branches.cn: 个人改掉坏习惯、改过自新

branches.en: Repaying the harm a fault has done
branches.cn: 弥补过错造成的伤害

branches.en: Correcting the faults of the earth itself
branches.cn: 改良土壤这类「修正大地」的用法

intro.en: Amend pairs the prefix a- with the fault root mend-, and regrows into amendments of every kind.
intro.cn: amend 由前缀 a- 加「缺陷」词根 mend- 构成，并衍生出各类「修正」词汇。

latinIntro.en: The Latin menda family keeps the idea of fault alive in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 menda 词族让「缺陷」的观念在英语中延续。

items.example: amender in French means to correct
items.exampleCN: 法语 amender 意为「改正」

items.example: emend means to drive the fault out

items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 sine menda 即「毫无瑕疵」

items.example: amendment is the act or result of amending
the report exposed the agency's mendacity
items.exampleCN: 报告揭露了该机构的谎言成性

items.meaning: a beggar; one with a flaw of need
items.meaningCN: 乞丐；托钵僧（词根关联存疑，一般认为同源）
